description:
You are an expert in TRNSYS energy system simulation. Please build a TRNSYS-based multi-zone office building HVAC simulation model using a packaged variable air volume (VAV) air handler with parallel fan powered (PFP) terminal boxes, direct expansion (DX) cooling, and electric resistance reheat to analyze the annual energy performance of a five-zone office building located in Boston, Massachusetts.

Simulation runs from hour 0 to hour 8760 (full year), with a time step of 5 minutes (5/60 hours). Integration and convergence tolerances are both set to 0.001, with a maximum of 30 iterations per time step.

Fluid properties for the loop: specific heat 4.19 kJ/(kg·K), density 1000 kg/m³, thermal conductivity 2.224 kJ/(h·m·K).

Weather data: The TMY3 weather file is provided at "D:\TRNSYS18_03\Examples\HVACTemplates\weather\US_MA_BOSTON_LOGAN_INTL_ARPT_725090.tmy3". The weather data processor reads this file and provides ambient dry bulb temperature, dew point temperature, relative humidity, effective sky temperature, wind velocity, atmospheric pressure, solar zenith and azimuth angles, ground reflectance, and tilted surface radiation data. One tilted surface is defined with a slope of 0° and azimuth of 0° (horizontal), using the Perez tilted surface radiation model (mode 5). Ground reflectance is set to 0.2.

Building model: The multi-zone building model configuration file is provided at "D:\TRNSYS18_03\Examples\HVACTemplates\buildings\ExampleBuilding_Sys6.b18". The building has 5 thermal zones: four lower-floor zones (LOWER1, LOWER2, LOWER3, LOWER4) each with a floor area of 150 m², and one upper-floor zone (UPPER) with a floor area of 400 m², totaling 1000 m². The star network calculation is performed only at the beginning of the simulation (switch = 0), and the operative temperature weighting factor is 0.50.

Outside convective heat transfer coefficient: Calculated using a wind-speed-dependent formula: h_outside = 3.6 × (3.8 × windSpeed_corr + 7.4) kJ/(h·m²·K), where windSpeed_corr = max(0, wind_speed) to eliminate negative values from the weather data file.

Internal heat gains: Lighting power density is 13 W/m² and equipment power density is 21.5 W/m². Occupancy density is calculated at one person per 20 m². Internal gains follow weekly schedules with three distinct daily profiles for occupancy and three for lighting/equipment:
- Weekday (Monday–Friday) occupancy: 0 from 0:00–7:00, ramps to 0.1 at 7:00, to 0.2 at 8:00, jumps to 0.95 at 9:00 and holds until 13:00, drops to 0.5 from 13:00–14:00, returns to 0.95 from 14:00–18:00, then decreases through 0.3 (18:00–19:00), 0.1 (19:00–23:00), and 0.05 (23:00–24:00).
- Saturday occupancy: 0 from 0:00–7:00, 0.1 from 7:00–9:00, 0.3 from 9:00–13:00, 0.1 from 13:00–18:00, 0.05 from 18:00–20:00, 0 from 20:00–24:00.
- Sunday occupancy: 0 from 0:00–7:00, 0.05 from 7:00–18:00, 0 from 18:00–24:00.
- Weekday lighting/equipment schedule: 0.05 from 0:00–5:00, 0.1 from 5:00–7:00, 0.3 from 7:00–8:00, 0.9 from 8:00–12:00, 0.8 from 12:00–13:00, 0.9 from 13:00–17:00, 0.5 from 17:00–18:00, 0.3 from 18:00–20:00, 0.2 from 20:00–22:00, 0.1 from 22:00–23:00, 0.05 from 23:00–24:00.
- Saturday lighting/equipment: 0.05 from 0:00–7:00, 0.1 from 7:00–9:00, 0.3 from 9:00–13:00, 0.15 from 13:00–17:00, 0.1 from 17:00–18:00, 0.05 from 18:00–24:00.
- Sunday lighting/equipment: constant at 0.05 throughout the day.
These daily profiles are assembled into weekly schedules using a forcing function sequencer that assigns Monday through Friday to the weekday profile, Saturday to the Saturday profile, and Sunday to the Sunday profile.

Outside air ventilation: Outside air flow rates are calculated using the ventilation rate procedure: 0.3 L/(s·m²) floor area plus 2.5 L/(s·person). For the four lower zones (150 m² each, 8 persons assumed), the required outside air is 65 L/s per zone. For the upper zone (400 m², 10 persons assumed), the required outside air is 145 L/s. The outside air fraction relative to the design air flow rate of 7510 L/s is dynamically calculated and modulated by a weekly schedule: on weekdays outside air is supplied from 8:00–17:00, on Saturdays from 8:00–17:00, and not on Sundays.

VAV air handler with parallel fan powered (PFP) terminal boxes: The central air handling unit serves all 5 zones and includes an economizer, a preheat coil, a cooling coil section, and a supply fan. Key parameters:
- Number of zones: 5
- Economizer: enabled
- Preheat coil: enabled
- Design dry air flow rate: 7510 L/s
- Fan performance data file: "D:\TRNSYS18_03\Examples\Data Files\Type151-FanLawPerformance.dat" with 11 part-load ratio data points
- Design fan power: 57600 kJ/h (approximately 16.0 kW)
- Specific heat of air: 1.007 kJ/(kg·K)
- Density of dry air: 1.2 kg/m³
- Minimum zonal air flow rates: 305, 305, 305, 305, 813 L/s (for LOWER1 through LOWER4 and UPPER respectively)
- Maximum zonal air flow rates: 917, 817, 1069, 921, 3786 L/s (for LOWER1 through LOWER4 and UPPER respectively)
- Zonal reheat coil capacity: -1 (unlimited) for all 5 zones
- Terminal box fan power: 446.4, 399.6, 522.0, 450.0, 1854.0 kJ/h (for LOWER1 through LOWER4 and UPPER respectively)
- Maximum cooling supply air temperature: 20.0°C (initial value)
- Minimum cooling supply air temperature: 12.78°C

Direct expansion (DX) cooling coil: An air-to-air DX coil is used as the cooling section of the air handler. It uses manufacturer's catalog data for performance modeling. Key parameters:
- Humidity mode: relative humidity mode (mode 2)
- Cooling performance data file: "D:\TRNSYS18_03\Examples\HVACTemplates\equipment\DXCoilCooling_260000.dat" with 6 outdoor dry-bulb temperature steps, 5 indoor dry-bulb temperature steps, 4 indoor wet-bulb temperature steps, and 3 air flow steps
- Heating performance data file: "D:\TRNSYS18_03\Examples\HVACTemplates\equipment\DXCoilHeating_notUsed.dat" (not actively used) with 16 outdoor dry-bulb temperature steps, 4 indoor temperature steps, and 3 air flow steps
- The DX coil cooling control signal is activated whenever the air handler's cooling coil heat transfer rate is greater than zero

Temperature control strategy:
- Heating setpoint: follows a weekly schedule — during occupied hours (weekdays 7:00–17:00) the setpoint is 21.1°C, during unoccupied hours the setpoint is 18.3°C
- Cooling setpoint: constant at 26.7°C throughout the year
- Maximum reheat supply air temperature: 35°C (used to calculate the maximum reheat coil capacity for each zone based on the formula: capacity = max_zone_airflow × 3600/1000 × air_density × Cp_air × (35 - zone_temperature), with a minimum of 0)

Delayed input controller: A delayed input device is used to hold 15 values from the previous time step and feed them back to the building model. These values include the unmet/additional sensible loads for each of the 5 zones, the latent addition rates for each zone, and the heating capacity limits for each zone. All values are delayed by 1 time step with initial values of 0.0. This feedback loop prevents simultaneous equation convergence issues between the air handler and the building model.

Output requirements:
- Plot zone air temperatures for all 5 zones along with the ambient dry bulb temperature, with Y-axis range from -30°C to 40°C. Generate approximately 52 plots per simulation (one per week, calculated as (STOP-START)/168).
- Generate hourly and monthly integrated energy reports including: AHU fan power, terminal unit fan power, DX coil power, preheat coil energy, reheat coil energy, total lighting load, and total equipment load. The hourly results are written to "***_hourly.out" and the monthly summaries to "***_monthly.out", with an integration interval of 1 hour.
